snp3.5:7.1: Following the Thai edition’s reading, alaggā (“unadhering”); the Burmese and PTS editions read asattā, “without attachment.”
snp3.5:21.1: In this verse, the Buddha is referring to himself.
snp3.5:24.5: A play on words: dosa means “fault” here, but “aversion” in the next line.
snp3.5:27.1: According to SnA, the threefold consummation of the sacrifice refers to the three qualities of the donor mentioned in AN 6:37—glad before giving, clear & bright-minded while giving, gratified after giving. But since this sutta doesn’t mention those qualities, that explanation is doubtful; more likely the reference is to the three points made just above: that the donor should clarify the mind, abandon the faults of passion & aversion, and develop immeasurable goodwill. See MN 97, AN 4:125–126, AN 10:196, and AN 11:16 on developing immeasurable goodwill.
